thesis: Next Generation Technology Group buys Japanese manufacturing companies and keeps them. The customers are the industrial buyers of the subsidiaries, which make parts and equipment and, in one case, rent and sell used forklifts. The parent does not run a single factory. It buys the whole company, usually for cash, and leaves the local name in place. It then tries to raise cash generation with a playbook it calls NGP. The shares trade on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Growth market as 319A.
why_market_wrong: The price already assumes a long run of further deals. On August 13, 2026 the company itself showed enterprise value at 47.3 times adjusted EBITDA, and the full-year forecast still excludes every acquisition closed in 2026. The half-year report and that forecast cannot both be the steady state. The open question is analytical: which earnings number a buyer is paying for.
